--Applicants vs State Of Uttarakhand
And Others on 5 June, 2025

Author: Rakesh Thapliyal Bench: Rakesh Thapliyal HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL  Anticipatory Bail Application No. 1186 of 2024  05 June, 2025 Vikas Narang and Others. --Applicants  Versus State Of Uttarakhand and Others

entities.text: Rakesh Thapliyal HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
entities.label: JUDGE

sentences.text:
Presence:
1. Mr. Samman Vardhan Gautam and Ms. Mamta Bisht, learned counsel for applicants.
2. Ms. Pushpa Bhatt, learned Additional Advocate General along with Mr.
V.S. Pal, learned AGA for the State.
3. Mr. Lalit Sharma, learned counsel for the respondent.
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J. (Oral)

The present anticipatory bail application has been moved by the applicants seeking anticipatory bail in relation to FIR dated 19.06.2024 bearing FIR No.0310 of 2024, Police Station Sidcul,
District-Haridwar, wherein the applicants have been implicated for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 468 and 506 IPC.

This First Information Report was earlier assailed in WPCRL No.731 of 2024, wherein the concerned Investigating Officer was directed to carry on with the investigation after following the procedure as prescribed under Section 41-A of Cr.P.C.

In the meantime, the account of the applicants' Firm was defreezed by the Bank pursuant to a notice dated 02.07.2024, then again WPCRL No.789 of 2024 was preferred before this Court, in which an affidavit was filed by the applicants, wherein it was contended that they are giving an undertaking to deposit an amount of Rs. 03 Crore and the said deposit will be subject to the outcome of the petition, for which two weeks' time was prayed.
In view of such an undertaking, the account of the applicants' Firm was defreezed.

2. Subsequently, a time extension application No.02 of 2024 was moved by the applicants seeking three months' time to deposit the amount as observed in the order dated 21.08.2024 and the time extension application was allowed and only six weeks' time was granted to the applicants to deposit the amount.

The order passed on time extension application dated 24.09.2024 is also being reproduced herein under:-
Vikas Narang And Others.

--Applicants vs State Of Uttarakhand And Others on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80889313/
1

" 4. Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioners would submit that the petitioners have filed Time Extension Application No.02/2024 seeking further three months time to deposit the balance amount as observed in the order dated 21.08.2024.

5. Learned counsel for respondent no.3 would submit that notwithstanding the fact that the petitioners have not honoured the undertaking given before the Court, but in the interest of justice, some more time may be given to the petitioners to deposit the amount.
6. In view of the above, six weeks more time is granted to the petitioners to deposit the amount of 3,00,00,000/- (Rupees Three Crores) as per order dated 21.08.2024.

Time Extension Application is disposed of."
3.

Despite the time extended for complying the order, another time extension was moved by the applicants i.e. IA No.05 of 2024 seeking six months' more additional time to deposit the amount of Rs. 3 Crore, however, the application was dismissed by observing that the same is misconceived.

The extract of the order is being reproduced herein as under:-
4. Heard on the Misc. Application (IA/5/2024) moved on behalf of petitioners seeking six months'
additional time to deposit the amount of Rs.3.00 crores pursuant to previous orders of the Court.

5. It appears from the record that vide order dated 21.08.2024, a Co-ordinate Bench of this Court, in view of undertaking filed in the form of affidavit, had permitted the petitioners to deposit the amount of Rs.3.00 crores by way of a bank draft in the Registry within two weeks from the date of order, and accordingly, the Branch Manager of the concerned Bank was directed to de-freeze the bank account of petitioners' firm which stood froze pursuant to the notice dated 02.07.2024.
6.

However, instead of depositing the amount, as undertaken, petitioners again knocked the door of the Court by moving time extension application (IA/2/2024), and a Co-ordinate Bench of this Court, by order dated 24.09.2024, granted further six weeks' time to the petitioners to deposit the said amount.
7. Now, by way of present application, petitioners have again sought six months' more time to deposit the amount.
8. From the aforesaid conduct of petitioners, it can safely be inferred that their intention is just to adopt the delay tactics by misleading the Court.

The same is quite apparent from the fact that since the date of first order dated 21.08.2024, time of almost four months has elapsed but they have not bothered to honour the undertaking given before this Court, and that too, which was in the form of an affidavit filed before the Court.
9. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, the application moved by petitioners (IA/5/2024) is misconceived and the same is, accordingly, dismissed.
Vikas Narang And Others.

--Applicants vs State Of Uttarakhand And Others on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80889313/
2
10. Resultantly, application (IA/4/2024) moved on behalf of respondent no.3 also stands disposed of.

11. Needless to mention at this stage that the natural consequences would follow in the matter."
Subsequently, the order passed on 10.07.2024 in WPCRL No.731 of 2024 was challenged before the Hon'ble Supreme Court by way of Special Leave to Appeal (CRL) No.13149 of 2024, wherein on 01.10.2024, the Hon'ble Apex Court passed the following orders:-
"UPON hearing the counsel the court made the following ORDER 1. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2.

entities.text: Special Leave to Appeal (CRL) No.13149 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Issue notice returnable within six weeks.
Mr. Arjun Singh Bharti, learned Advocate on-Record appears on caveat on behalf of respondentNo.3, formal notice to the said respondent is accordingly, waived.

3. In the meantime, it is provided that no coercive steps shall be taken against the petitioner, provided the petitioner shall abide by the undertaking given to the High Court and deposits the amount before the High Court within the time allowed and upon deposit of the said amount, it shall be invested in an interest bearing account in a Nationalized Bank."
Subsequently the complainant intervened before the Hon'ble Apex Court, and, thereafter, on 20.11.2024, the Hon'ble Supreme Court dismissed the SLP.

The order passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court dated 20.11.2024 is also being reproduced herein as under:-
"Heard learned counsel for the parties.
This special leave petition is directed against the order dated 10.07.2024 passed by the High Court of Uttarakhand at Nainital (briefly 'the High Court').

entities.text: High Court of Uttarakhand at Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Relevant portion of the said order reads as under:
4. By the instant writ petition, the petitioners are praying for quashing of the FIR dated 19.06.2024, bearing FIR No.0310 of 2024 at P.S. SIDCUL, Haridwar wherein the petitioners have been implicated for the offences punishable under Sections 406,
420, 468 and 506 IPC.
5.

On the previous date, the State was directed to apprise this Court about the criminal history of the petitioners and on instruction Mr. Pratiroop Pandey, learned A.G.A. for the State informed to this Court that there is no criminal history of the petitioners.
He further submits that investigation is going on and all the offences are punishable upto seven years and notice under Section 41-A Cr.P.C. has been given to the petitioners.
He further submits that the 1.0. is not intended to arrest the Vikas Narang And Others.

--Applicants vs State Of Uttarakhand And Others on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80889313/
3 petitioners at this stage since the investigation is still going on.

6. Since, all the offences are punishable upto seven years, therefore, investigation may go on pursuant to the impugned FIR and the 1.0. concerned may follow the procedure as prescribed under Section 41A Cr.P.C.
7.
In view of the above direction as given, the writ petition is disposed of."

It may be mentioned that petitioners had submitted before the High Court in another proceeding relating to the same F.I.R. being Writ Petition (Crl.) No. 789 of 2024 on 21.08.2024 that he would deposit an amount of Rs. 3 crores.

Considering the above, this Court vide order dated 01.10.2024 had issued notice and had directed in the interim that no coercive steps shall be taken against the petitioners subject to depositing the aforesaid amount before the High Court.
Today, learned counsel for the petitioners submits that petitioners are not in a position to deposit Rs. 3 crores.
He has brought a Demand Draft for an amount of Rs. 25,00,000/- (Rupees twenty-five lakhs) only.
This means that petitioners have not complied with the order of this Court dated 01.10.2024.

Considering the conduct of the petitioners as well as the order of the High Court dated 10.07.2024,
we are not inclined to interfere further in this matter.
The special leave petition is, accordingly, dismissed.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of."

Subsequently when the order was not complied with despite the fact that the period was extended on a time extension application moved by the applicants then I.A. No.06 of 2024 was moved by the complainant for recalling the earlier order dated 21.08.2024 in which, on an undertaking of the applicants, the account of the applicants' Firm was defreezed and on such an application, this Court on 09.01.2025 again freezed the account of the applicants.
The relevant extracts of this order is being reproduced herein as under.

14. Admittedly on perusal of the order passed by this Court as well as by the Hon'ble Supreme Court,
it reveals that the petitioners obtained the order of de-freezing the account by giving false undertaking.

15. In such an eventuality, to examine the issue whether petitioners have committed the fraud with this Court or not and whether it amounts to contempt or not, the notices are being issued to the petitioners to show-cause within four weeks, why they may not be prosecuted by giving false undertaking before this Court and be not punished under the provisions under the Contempt of Courts Act.
Vikas Narang And Others.
--Applicants vs State Of Uttarakhand And Others on 5 June, 2025

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80889313/
4 16.

Whether petitioners have played fraud or not with this Court, this question can be examined by the Regular Bench, but, this Court, prima facie, is of the view that the petitioners have given the false undertaking before this Court and obtained the order of defreezing the account.

17. In such an eventuality, since by the present IA No. 6 of 2024 (Criminal Miscellaneous Application), the respondent-complainant is seeking recalling the order dated 21.08.2024 and since,
undisputedly, the petitioners give a false undertaking before this Court, therefore, the account which was defreezed by the order dated 21.08.2024 is directed to be freezed with immediate effect."

4. Against the order dated 09.01.2025 passed in IA No.06 of 2024, the applicants again approached to the Hon'ble Apex Court, but the counsel for the applicants apprise to this Court that the SLP was withdrawn, thereafter, another application was moved in WPCRL No.789 of 2024 by the applicants,
which was dismissed and now for initiating action against the applicants for giving false undertakings before this Court, the proceedings are going on before the Coordinate Bench.
5.
Put up this matter before the appropriate Bench along with WPCRL No.789 of 2024 next week.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 05.06.2025 R.Bisht Vikas Narang And Others.

--Applicants vs State Of Uttarakhand And Others on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80889313/
